newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt approves draft on farming policy.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt approves draft on farming policy.

text.p: Hungary's government approved the first version of a medium-term farming policy, spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.
"All cabinet ministers approved the draft," Kiss said after the cabinet meeting, where few details of the plan were released.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn appointed Frigyes Nagy as agriculture minister last December after sacking his predecessor, Laszlo Lakos.
Horn said Nagy's main task was to prepare Hungary's agriculture for European Union membership.
Kiss said the draft will allow companies to purchase farmland for green field investments only but would at the same allow land to be leased for up to 40 years.
He added that any company registered in Hungary would have the same rights.
He added, however, that the government does not intend to allow foreigners to own land.
Present legislation limits land ownership to 300 hectares and bans foreigners from owning land.
Kiss did not give further details of the draft, which will now be open for public debate, but said Nagy would present it to journalists on Friday.
